guide.heading: Master Your Time with the Pomodoro Technique
guide.intro: The Pomodoro Technique is a time-management method developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s. It uses a timer to break down work into intervals, traditionally 25 minutes in length, separated by short breaks.
guide.step1Desc: Choose what you want to accomplish from your task list. Keep your focus on that task only.
guide.step2Desc: Start the timer and work with undivided attention until the bell chimes. Avoid all distractions.
guide.step3Desc: Step away from your screen. Stretch, drink water, or take deep breaths to recharge your mind.
guide.step4Desc: After every 4 completed pomodoros, reward yourself with a restorative 15-30 minute break.
guide.faq1Q: Why is the Pomodoro technique so effective?
guide.faq1A: It creates a sense of urgency, limits multitasking, and prevents cognitive fatigue by encouraging regular rest periods.
guide.faq2Q: Will my tasks and settings be saved if I close the tab?
guide.faq2A: Yes! All tasks, theme preferences, and timer settings are securely saved in your local browser storage.
guide.faq3Q: Does the timer keep running if I switch tabs?
guide.faq3A: Yes. PomoFocus Pro uses a Web Worker and timestamp synchronization so the timer never loses precision in background tabs.
